title: How Software Works
tagline: Web, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, your first API
goal: Build the mental model of how the web works and ship a first live page with real data. For trainees with no web background.
audience: Complete beginners with no web background.
skippable: Week 0 can be skipped by passing the test-out before Day 1. Test-out (2 hours, no AI, mentor present): build a responsive page, fetch data from a public API through a search box (for example, Open-Meteo weather by city), push it to GitHub, explain what happens when a URL is typed into the browser, and solve two of the Week 0 Day 4 console drills.
outcomes: Explain the URL-to-page flow (DNS, TCP/TLS, HTTP, render) out loud in 2 minutes
Write semantic, accessible HTML with working forms
Build responsive layouts from 360px to 1440px with Flexbox, Grid and media queries
Write DOM-manipulating JavaScript with event delegation and no globals
Call a real API with fetch, handling loading, error and empty states
Debug with DevTools: Elements, Console, Network, Sources
Ship a portfolio to GitHub Pages
projectStage: No booking product yet. You are building the muscles: HTML, CSS, JS, fetch, Git. Week 0 has no PRs, so explain-back runs on the day's last commit and 'How I verified this' goes in the README.

days.title: How the Web Works + Setup
learn: What happens when a URL is typed (DNS, server, HTTP request, response, render)
Client vs server; what frontend, backend, database and API mean
Terminal basics (cd, ls, mkdir), files and folders, relative vs absolute paths
VS Code, Live Server, Git + GitHub
Browser DevTools: Elements, Console, Network
tasks: Install VS Code, Git, Node.js and an AI coding tool (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode). Set up ChatGPT or Claude as a tutor for the mornings. Create a GitHub account.
Open any real website, list every request in the Network tab and label each one (HTML, CSS, JS, image, API call).
Draw the URL-to-page flow on paper or in Excalidraw.
Set up a project folder with index.html, styles/ and images/.
Open the page through Live Server and through file:// and note the difference.
Create a repo, make a first commit and push it.
acceptance: Can explain the URL-to-page flow out loud in 2 minutes.
First repo is on GitHub with at least one commit.
No broken asset paths.

days.title: HTML + Forms
learn: Semantic tags (header, nav, main, section, article, footer), headings, lists, links, images, alt text
Forms, labels, input types, textarea, select, buttons, required fields
Keyboard navigation
tasks: Build a profile page with a heading, intro, image, skills list and nav.
Add a contact form with name, email and message.
Fill the whole form using only the keyboard.
acceptance: One h1, and heading levels follow a logical order.
Every image has meaningful alt text. Every input has a label.
Page passes validator.w3.org.
Browser blocks submit on empty required fields or an invalid email.

days.title: CSS + Responsive Layout
learn: Selectors, specificity, box model, units (px, rem, %), typography, colors
Flexbox, Grid, media queries, mobile-first, responsive images
Hover, focus and active states
tasks: Style the profile page from an external stylesheet.
Add a 3-card project grid that stacks on mobile.
Add a 2-column layout (content + sidebar) that also stacks on mobile.
Add hover, active and focus states to buttons and links.
acceptance: No inline styles.
Clean layout from 360px to 1440px with no horizontal scroll.
Focus is visible when tabbing, and hover, active and focus states look distinct.

days.title: JavaScript + DOM
learn: const/let, types, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, scope, truthy/falsy
Arrays (push, pop, slice, splice, indexOf, includes), objects, nested data
The DOM tree, querySelector/querySelectorAll, creating and removing elements, textContent vs innerHTML, classList
Events: addEventListener, the event object, preventDefault, bubbling, event delegation, input vs change vs submit
Loading scripts with type="module" (works on Live Server, not file://)
tasks: Morning drills (by hand, in the console): reverse a string, FizzBuzz, count words in a string, a number guessing game (1-100), a grade calculator that turns a 0-100 score into a letter grade.
Render the project cards from a JavaScript array of objects (create elements instead of hardcoding HTML).
Add a filter that shows project cards by tag, using one delegated click listener on the card list.
acceptance: No var, no inline JavaScript, no global variables.
Works without a page reload, zero console errors.
User text is rendered with textContent (no injection).
One listener on the card list, not one per card.
Data functions handle empty arrays and missing fields without crashing.

days.title: First API Call
learn: JSON, fetch, Promises, async/await, HTTP status codes
Loading, error and empty states
Date basics, localStorage, JSON.stringify/parse, try/catch
tasks: Add a live weather widget using Open-Meteo (no API key needed): find the city with the geocoding API (geocoding-api.open-meteo.com), then show current weather + a 5-day forecast with readable dates, and an empty state when no city matches.
Show a loading state, an error state with a Retry button, and the data.
Save the last 5 searched cities as a JSON array in localStorage and show them as quick links.
Find the request in the Network tab.
acceptance: Can explain the request's URL, method, status code and response body.
With the network off, the error state shows (not a blank widget).
Non-2xx responses are treated as errors.
Corrupted search history falls back to an empty list.

days.title: Debug Lab (no AI)
learn: Inspecting and live-editing styles, device toolbar
Reading Console errors, Network tab for 404s
Console methods (log, table, error)
Breakpoints and step-through in the Sources panel
brokenLab: A CSS specificity bug (style not applying)
A card that overflows on mobile
A form input with no label
A fetch call that fails silently
A click handler attached twice, so one click fires two actions and duplicates items
tasks: The runnable broken page is in the repository at labs/week-0/broken (see labs/README.md). Fix it using DevTools only, then check with: node labs/week-0/check.mjs broken
Fix all six bugs in the provided broken page, using only DevTools and your own reasoning.
acceptance: All six fixed, zero console or network errors.
Each fix written up as: symptom → cause → fix → how verified.

days.title: Weekly Project: Personal Portfolio Site
tasks: About section, projects grid (3+ cards), contact form, live API widget.
Dark mode toggle saved in localStorage (corrupted data falls back to the default) and a live character counter on the message field.

Contact form handled in JavaScript: novalidate, preventDefault, your own validation messages with checkValidity(), a success message, and no page reload. An empty or invalid field shows your message and nothing is submitted.
Fully responsive from 360px to 1440px.
Pushed to GitHub, deployed on GitHub Pages, README with screenshots.
acceptance: See the rubric on the Project tab.

project.name: Personal Portfolio Site

Pushed to GitHub, deployed on GitHub Pages, README with screenshots
stretch: A page that lists your public repos from the GitHub API.
